headline: Driverless fleet scales up, but losses widen and cash drops
summary_short: Revenue rose to $2M (+100% q/q and y/y) on record commercial miles as Aurora launched its second-generation driverless fleet, but the operating loss widened to $266M and cash and equivalents fell to $136M ($1.2B including short-term investments).
summary_long: Revenue grew to $2M on record commercial miles as Aurora launched its second-generation driverless fleet and signed new TaaS agreements with Charger Logistics, Value Truck, and Volvo Autonomous Solutions. Operating loss widened to $266M (R&D $211M, SG&A $50M) as headcount and hardware costs scaled ahead of commercialization; operating cash use was $225M and capex $31M. A $215M net ATM raise lifted liquidity, but cash and equivalents fell to $136M ($1.2B including short-term investments). Aurora reaffirmed FY2026 revenue guidance of $14-16M (+400% y/y at midpoint), expects to exit the year with 200+ driverless trucks (~$80M TaaS run-rate), and continues to guide quarterly cash use of $190-220M with ~$150M of FY2026 capex.

drivers.explanation: Aurora entered its commercial scaling phase — launching driverless Aurora Driver 2 trucks and signing new TaaS customers — while operating losses widened as R&D and SG&A scaled ahead of 2027's planned DaaS ramp.
Revenue came from driverless and vehicle-operator-supervised commercial loads, with the Aurora Driver achieving a record number of commercial miles during the quarter.
Loss from operations widened as R&D rose to $211M and SG&A to $50M, reflecting scaled headcount and hardware spend ahead of full driverless commercialization.
Net loss widened on the larger operating loss plus a $32M unfavorable swing in the fair value of derivative liabilities versus the year-ago quarter.
Cash and equivalents fell as ATM proceeds were partly used for $63M of cash bonus payments and RSU tax withholding, with the remainder held in short-term investments rather than cash.
Share count rose after Aurora issued 30 million Class A shares through its at-the-market program during the quarter.
